name: Boost
author: David JM
description: Limit your CPU's max boost clock straight from the bar, with optional thermal protection, temporary MAX boosts, and live CPU telemetry.

barWidget.description: A bolt glyph showing the current max boost cap. Left-click opens a slider, presets, Thermal Guard, temporary MAX boost countdowns, and live frequency/power/utilization graphs. Changes apply through the separately installed root-owned helper and persist across reboots; right-click cycles presets and middle-click refreshes the live reading.

schema.label: Max boost (GHz)
schema.description: Max boost cap. Set live with the popup slider (any 1.0–5.0 GHz value); the last-applied value is persisted and re-applied by the cpu-cap-boost.service systemd unit on boot.

schema.label: Presets (comma-separated)
schema.description: Custom preset chips and right-click cycle steps. Empty (default) = auto-generated for the CPU: BASE, evenly-spaced steps up to MAX, so the chips fit the chip's reported range. Tokens: 'base', 'max', or any GHz value like 3.5. Also editable in the popup.

schema.label: Manual max boost (GHz)
schema.description: Pin the usable max-boost ceiling to a fixed value, e.g. 4.7 for a CPU that a PBO BIOS reports higher than its rated max. Blank = trust the CPU's own reported max. Never exceeds the CPU's sysfs max.

schema.label: Base clock (GHz)
schema.description: Manual base clock for the panel and the BASE preset, e.g. 3.8, when sysfs can't report it (acpi-cpufreq Ryzen without CPPC exposes no base_frequency). Blank = auto-detect.

schema.label: Thermal Guard
schema.description: Automatically lower the CPU cap when the package temperature reaches the trigger threshold. The guard releases only after the package stays below the release threshold for the cooldown period.

schema.label: Thermal Guard trigger (°C)
schema.description: Package temperature at which Thermal Guard engages.

schema.label: Thermal Guard release (°C)
schema.description: Package temperature below which Thermal Guard can begin its cooldown release. Must be lower than the trigger.

schema.label: Thermal Guard cap (GHz)
schema.description: Maximum CPU cap used while Thermal Guard is latched. It is still clamped to the CPU's reported hardware ceiling.

schema.label: Thermal Guard cooldown (seconds)
schema.description: Time the package must remain below the release threshold before the normal cap is restored.

schema.label: Temporary boost duration (minutes)
schema.description: Default duration for the temporary MAX boost button. The active countdown continues in the background and restores the latest manual cap when it expires.

schema.label: Live CPU graphs
schema.description: Collect and display live frequency, package power, and CPU utilization graphs when the Boost monitor is available.
